title: Magical Girl Dandelion
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: High schooler Tanpopo Ohanami, raised by her grandfather after fiends killed her parents, is close friends with Shade, a shadowy fiend who saved her as a child. When she becomes a magical girl, whose job is to fight villains like him, their bond is tested, and she begins to question who decides what makes a 'good' magical girl (Viz blurb; ANN Spring 2026 Manga Guide).
life_message: Love, not hate, is the true source of strength, and labels of good and evil deserve questioning.

content.note: 'Fairly bloody violence' though 'not as grimdark' as genre peers (ANN); MU Blood and Gore; swords and guns.
Fiends killed her parents; body horror listed as a spoiler tag (ANN; AniList Body Horror).
Close, teasing bond with a protective fiend (MU Teasing Male Lead, Protective Male Lead); reviewers do not mention romance (to verify).
Viz rates it T; nothing noted.
Genre conventions of transformation and cute mascots (MU Monster Sidekick/s).

dominant: Love over hate; questioning institutional labels of good and evil; loyalty across sides

frames.aligns: Tanpopo's love as the source of power; loyalty to a friend.
frames.concerns: A sympathetic fiend may blur good and evil.
Demon-like fiend portrayed as a beloved protector.
Magic and a friendly demon figure.
Demonic figure as heroine's dearest friend.
Moral lines blurred around a fiend.

frames.aligns: Love for neighbor, even across sides.
Light and dark themes framed seriously.
Love rather than hate as the true power.
Girl who 'thinks for herself' against an institution.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Fights driven by protection, not insult (ANN).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Tanpopo thinks for herself against the organization (ANN).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Questions who runs the magical-girl organization (ANN).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Love as personal source of power (ANN).

folkways.japan: A shoujo magical-girl story; the grandfather raising an orphan reflects common Japanese family patterns.

delivery.evidence: ANN reviewers praise twists and independent thinking; none call it preachy.

personified.ideology: Magical girls fueled by love rather than hate

delivery.note: The genre's good-versus-evil framing is questioned through plot twists; the organization's side is not yet fully shown.

winners_losers: Tanpopo and Shade's bond gets sympathy; the institution that labels heroes and villains is cast in doubt.
to_verify: Whether the Tanpopo and Shade bond becomes romantic.
Body horror and gore levels in later volumes (spoiler tags).
